Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Oil & Gas Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Oil & Gas Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; David Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Operating Officer; Alex Rivera, VP of Exploration; and Lisa Chen, VP of Marketing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Apex Oil & Gas delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust EBITDA growth year-over-year, fueled by higher realized pricing and production volumes. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on midstream segment performance, where transportation volumes hit records and infrastructure projects advanced ahead of schedule. We are focused on exploration and drilling activities, with standout well results from key pads and clear plans for acceleration. Further, we are working on proved reserves additions, boasting a superior reserve replacement ratio through organic growth. We continue to adjust to prudent debt management, with meaningful reductions in total and net debt alongside improving leverage ratios. Finally, we are taking steps to drive down operating expenses per BOE through aggressive cost controls and efficiency gains.

Now, I'll turn the call over to David Patel to discuss our financial results in more detail.

David Patel: Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $4.5 billion, up 25% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.1 billion, and net income was $850 million. We generated $1.1 billion in free cash flow and returned $500 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $4.8 billion in debt and $1.4 billion in cash.

Let me expand on our EBITDA performance first, which reached $1.8 billion for the quarter—a solid 28% increase from $1.4 billion in the same period last year. Looking at the trailing twelve months, adjusted EBITDA hit $6.8 billion, reflecting a 24% year-over-year rise that beat the midpoint of our guidance and highlighted the resilience of our integrated operations even in fluctuating markets.

The primary drivers included stronger realized pricing, where our blended price per barrel of oil equivalent rose to $78.50 per BOE, an 18% jump from $66.50 a year earlier. Brent crude averaged $82 per barrel during the period, about $12 higher than last year, supported by ongoing OPEC+ production cuts and strong global demand, especially from Asia-Pacific refineries recovering post-COVID. Natural gas prices also advanced to $3.25 per MCF from $2.80, with Henry Hub above $3 per MMBTU due to seasonal LNG exports. Roughly 75% of our oil output was hedged at a $75 per barrel floor using collars and swaps, securing about $4 million daily in protected cash flow while capturing upside.

Production volumes grew as well, averaging 525,000 BOE per day, up 7% from 490,000 BOE per day last year. U.S. onshore assets led, with Permian Basin output at a record 320,000 BOE per day, a 12% increase. This stemmed from longer laterals and improved completions—in the Delaware Basin, 10,000-foot laterals with 55 stages per well delivered initial rates 25% higher at over 1,500 BOE per day, with drilled and completed costs below $7 million, on par with competitors. The Waha gas plant expansion's first phase added 200 MMcf per day of processing to handle associated gas more effectively.

Internationally, the North Sea's Buzzard field saw 15% production growth to 85,000 BOE per day through subsea tie-backs and AI reservoir modeling, dropping lease operating expenses to $8.50 per BOE with over 95% uptime. In Guyana analogs at Block Z, first oil from our Petronas-partnered FPSO contributed 25,000 barrels per day at over $85 per barrel realizations and breakevens under $35 per barrel. Middle East joint ventures grew 5% despite higher royalties, leading to 4% overall non-U.S. production growth.

Cost control played a big role too, holding upstream DD&A steady at $12 per BOE despite higher volumes, thanks to a 140% reserve replacement from low-cost sources. Lifting costs declined 10% to $9.20 per BOE via supply chain deals like frac sand at $25 per ton and digital twins on 40 rigs that reduced non-productive time 18% with predictive tools. Midstream margins widened 300 basis points to 45%, powered by 95% utilization at our Eagle Ford NGL unit amid $15 per barrel cracks at Mont Belvieu.

This growth supports our capital discipline, with 65% of $2.2 billion capex directed to Permian and offshore assets for 6-8% organic growth next year and FCF yields over 15% at $70 Brent. We hedged 50% of 2024 oil at $72 per barrel floors, repurchased $400 million in shares under our $1.5 billion program, and raised the dividend 12% recently, returning 40% of cash flow. Headwinds like a $150 million FX hit from a strong USD on Norwegian revenues and 200 basis point downstream margin squeeze to $5.50 per barrel from turnarounds were more than offset.

Overall, this positions us for $7.0 to $7.4 billion full-year EBITDA, with upside from 5,000 Permian locations at sub-$40 breakevens and Gulf Coast LNG deals.

Shifting to proved reserves, we added 285 million BOE for full-year 2023, lifting year-end totals to 2.8 billion BOE and delivering a 142% reserve replacement ratio against 201 million BOE produced—above our 120% target and marking the third straight year over 130%, with a three-year average of 138% that ranks top quartile versus EOG at 125% and Pioneer at 132%.

Ninety-two percent, or 262 million BOE, came organically from our drillbit efforts, minimizing acquisition reliance amid pricey deals like Occidental's. Only 23 million BOE were inorganic from DJ Basin tuck-ins.

In the Permian, 145 million BOE replaced 115% of production across 450,000 net acres, with laterals over 12,000 feet boosting EUR to 1.8 million BOE per well; PDP added 92 million BOE, PUD 53 million from 4,500 sub-$40 breakeven spots.

Eagle Ford hit 165% RRR with 68 million BOE added versus 41 million produced, via refracs on verticals adding 15-20% EUR and 22 million BOE revisions from fiber-optic monitoring.

Gulf of Mexico added 42 million BOE, including PUD from Lightning via advanced seismic, with 60% oil and $50 per BOE netbacks at $80 Brent.

Suriname Block 58 with TotalEnergies booked 30 million BOE from Roystonea-1X, sanctioning Phase 1 at 50,000 barrels per day gross.

Tech drove it: 18% drilling efficiency gains to 8 days per well in Permian, 25% IP lifts to 1,400 BOE per day with optimized completions, and AI simulations yielding $150 million revisions.

This insulates us with 14-year inventory life, targeting 140%+ RRR in 2024 with 70% capex to Tier 1 drilling and ESG methane cuts aiding PUD conversions.

On debt levels, total debt stood at $4.8 billion at quarter-end, down 21% from $6.1 billion a year ago, thanks to $850 million Q3 free cash flow from Permian assets at 145,000 BOE per day and sub-$7 million well costs.

Long-term debt is $4.2 billion: $1.5 billion 4.125% notes due 2029 refinanced from 5.25%, and $2.7 billion term loans. Short-term and revolver draws are $600 million, reduced $450 million from Eagle Ford cash.

We tendered $500 million 2026 notes for $25 million annual savings and eye more refis as HY spreads tighten 150 bps.

Net debt is $3.4 billion, down 24% sequentially and 29% YoY, with $1.4 billion cash boosted by $300 million Bakken sales at $22,000 per acre.

Leverage improved: net debt to LTM EBITDAX at 1.4x from 2.1x YoY, with $2.45 billion LTM from 65% Permian margins. Gross debt/EBITDAX 2.0x, debt-to-cap 28%, 4.1x interest coverage, 650 bps covenant headroom.

This matches low-end peers like Diamondback at 1.2x, enabling 65% 2025 oil hedges at $75 floors.

We'll hit sub-$3 billion net debt by year-end via $2.2 billion FCF at $75-80 WTI, reallocating capex to Permian IRRs over 60%, monetizing $400 million Rockies, and pursuing $1 billion green bonds tied to methane cuts.

Operating expenses per BOE totaled $8.45 in Q3, down 8% YoY from $9.20 and 4% sequentially from Q4, the fifth straight quarter of declines and 20% below our five-year average, landing lower quartile versus Permian peers.

TTM trend: from $11.20 peak in 2022 to $9.10 in 2023, guiding $7.90-$8.30 for 2024 full-year, another 10-13% drop. Breakdown: LOE $5.20 (-9% YoY via automation), G&T $2.15 (-10% via contracts), taxes $0.85 flat, workovers $0.25 flat—leveraged by 15% production growth to 525,000 BOE per day.

Permian at $7.20 per BOE (-12% YoY), with 1,200 BOE per day wells, sub-$1.80 G&T on owned pipes. Eagle Ford $10.50 (+2% on water costs, targeting 70% recycle). Bakken $9.80 flat, with pipeline efficiencies.

Strategies include Digital Oilfield with Halliburton AI cutting downtime 25% and workovers to $0.25; drones slashing LOE $0.40; analytics saving $15 million on chemicals. SLB/Baker contracts 5% below prior, renewables dropping diesel $0.20, cube dev under $400 per foot, shared services $50 million savings.

Outlook: scale to 550,000 BOE per day, commodity support, service deflation target $7 per BOE by 2026 for 20% FCF yield.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins for an operational update.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, David. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 525,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Blackhawk pad online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

Focusing on midstream, this segment provided stable fee-based cash flows, de-risking our upstream amid volatility. Transportation volumes averaged 2.8 million BOE per day, up 18% year-over-year and 7% sequentially—our ninth straight double-digit growth quarter from Permian surges and basin positioning.

Crude oil hit 1.65 million barrels per day, +22% YoY; Permian on EPIC at 850,000 barrels per day, 92% utilized, with WTI Midland basis at $0.75 discount. Bakken 320,000 barrels per day on Dakota Access, +15%.

Natural gas 4.2 Bcf per day, +14%; Haynesville 1.8 Bcf per day for LNG. NGLs/refined 550,000 barrels per day, +12%, fractionating 75% in-house.

Utilization 88%, tariffs $425 million +21% at $0.42 per barrel-mile, backed by take-or-pay with Exxon and Oxy.

Infrastructure capex $1.2 billion YTD toward $4.5 billion full-year. Permian Highway Pipeline Phase III (550 miles, 42-inch, 2.2 Bcf per day) mechanically complete, commissioning Q4, 95% contracted to Chevron/EQT for LNG. EPIC NGL Connect added 150,000 barrels per day ethane rejection. Rockies reversal 120 miles for 180,000 barrels per day DJ crude, 20%+ IRR.

Permian 55% of EBITDA, mitigating Waha -$0.25 with compression. Appalachia Utica +10% paced carefully. AI analytics cut downtime 25%, deferring $50 million capex; electrified segments -40% emissions; drone ILI 30% faster.

Midstream EBITDA $650 million +25% YoY, 72% margins. Q4 volumes 2.95 million BOE per day, full-year +19%, $2.6 billion EBITDA reaffirmed with $15 billion backlog. 90% fee-based, 65% 2025 tolls hedged.

Now I will turn it over to Alex Rivera for an update on our exploration activities.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and are planning to drill 30 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

In Q3, we spudded 28 wells, brought 32 online, and turned 25 to sales, up 15% sequentially, running 4.2 rigs with days per well down 8% to 18 via pad/walk-up. E&D capex $450 million, 65% of upstream, on track for 120-130 wells year-end, IP30 averaging 1,450 BOE per day, 12% above type curves—at $82 WTI, $2.85 Henry Hub.

Permian 85% activity, 22 wells in northern Delaware/southern Midland, 3,200 locations over 11,000-foot laterals. Blackhawk 12H-15H pad in Lea County: Wolfcamp A/B IP30 1,850 BOE per day (82% oil), peaks 3,200, 25% above curve with 110 lbs/ft proppant, diverters; EUR 1.8 million BOE, breakevens <$35, costs $7.2 million/$650 ft. Midland Rattlesnake 7H-10H 1,200 IP30 (70% oil), multi-zone stacking +20-30% EUR. Differentials $1.50 under WTI, flaring <1%.

Eagle Ford 10%, Dorado 22H 18 MMcf/d IP30 (15% condensate), EUR 4.2 Bcfe +18% via super-zipper fracs; costs $6.8 million, 100%+ half-cycle at $3 gas. Permitted 150 more for LNG tailwinds.

Gulf of Mexico Albatross #1 120 ft net oil, DST 4,500 bbl/d +12 MMcf/d, de-risking 500 million BOE; $120 million capex, 30% carry. Namibia Orange Basin spud with Galp, 2 billion barrel potential.

Tech: ML with Halliburton DecisionPoint -15% frac hits; 100% ceramic proppants +20% conductivity; data science up-ranks 400 spots. Electrified fracs -25% emissions, 90% water recycle.

2025: 140-160 wells, $1.8-2.0 billion capex, 75% Permian for 20% inventory to 3,500; +1 Midland rig at $80+ WTI; Stack bolt-ons post $300 million Howard deal.

98% success, resilient inventory 85% oil <$45 breakevens.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Lisa Chen to discuss our marketing strategy.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Alex. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for NGLs in the Mont Belvieu market area, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of these efforts on our realizations and margins is significant, capturing premiums through hedging and long-term contracts while navigating basis volatility.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Joe Harris with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Joe Harris: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the key drivers behind your EBITDA outperformance this quarter?

Mike Thompson: Good morning, Joe. Absolutely, as David outlined, the 28% lift came from $78.50 per BOE realizations—18% higher on $82 Brent and better gas—plus 7% volume growth to 525,000 BOE per day led by Permian records. Hedging locked in value, costs stayed disciplined with LOE down 10%, and international assets like Buzzard and Guyana added tailwinds despite some FX noise. This operational leverage sets us up well.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Good morning. What are your expectations for debt reduction and leverage ratios into next year?

David Patel: Good morning, Emily. We're on track to sub-$3 billion net debt by year-end with $2.2 billion FCF, targeting 1.0x or better net debt to EBITDAX. Continued revolver paydowns, asset sales like Rockies, and capex focus on high-IRR Permian will drive it, while refis and green bonds keep costs low. Our 1.4x now gives plenty of firepower.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly: Could you please provide more color on operating expenses per BOE trends and your cost strategies?

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning, Tom. OPEX at $8.45 per BOE marks ongoing deflation—8% YoY—with LOE and G&T down double-digits via digital tools cutting downtime 25%, drone inspections, renewables, and contracts below inflation. Permian efficiencies shine at $7.20, and we'll hit $7.90-$8.30 full-year through scale and zero-based budgeting, targeting $7 by 2026.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Alex Rivera: Good morning, Rachel. Standouts like Blackhawk's 1,850 BOE per day IP30 and Albatross de-risking validate accelerating Permian to 75% of 2025 capex for 3,500 locations, while Eagle Ford gas feeds LNG growth and offshore pilots add optionality. This boosts PDP replacement to 8-10% annually, supporting dividend hikes without major M&A.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Lopez with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Mark Lopez: What is the outlook for NGL products in the coming years?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Mark. Strong Mont Belvieu demand drives our NGL push, with expansions like EPIC Connect boosting margins 15% and 95% utilization capturing cracks. We'll grow volumes 12-15% annually via Eagle Ford feeds, long-term petrochemical offtakes, and basis hedging, contributing steady high-margin cash amid LNG ramps.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
